remainingEvidence: The reachability conjunct is built and partly tested, so what remains here is narrower than construction: src/facets/runtime.ts#OperationContext declares a required `signal: AbortSignal`, and a Turn's cancellation reaches it through the scope signal TurnExecutor hands its executor, GatewayTurnInvocationPort's TurnGatewayScope, ComposedTurnGatewaySource.open calling operations(scope.signal), and the shared { signal, content } resources both DerivedDirectOperationContext and CanonicalBatchInvocationPort put on the handler's context. test/composition/mediation-pipeline.test.ts already discriminates the never-abort substitute over the concrete pipeline — 'the published mediation composition root runs each Operation under its own Turn's cancellation signal' asserts the handler's observed context signal is identically the Turn's signal and that an already-aborted Turn signal prevents dispatch with zero handler calls — but it carries no atom tag, so it is not yet conformance evidence for this row under scripts/quality/ledger.mjs's priority-evidence rule

What no test does is abort a Turn while an Operation handler is suspended and observe that handler's own context signal fire: the pipeline case aborts before invoke and then uses a controller it never aborts, and the only mid-execution abort observation in the suite is on a facet `start` hook's FacetLifecycleContext in test/operations/runtime.test.ts, not on an OperationContext. Availability at handler entry and observability during handler execution are different claims, and this rule makes the second one

The distinction this rule exists for is untested: an attempt whose wait the host abandoned must record `indeterminate` while an attempt whose handler observed its context cancellation must record `aborted` under C13-RECEIPT-FAILURE-KIND, and a mutation substituting a never-abort sentinel for the context signal must collapse the second case into the first rather than leaving both green

Propagation past the seam has no enforcement point at all. Nothing requires a handler that awaits further asynchronous work under its own invocation's lifetime to pass its context cancellation on, and nothing keeps a bound it derives linked to the cancellation it derived from. Closure needs a profile handler that delegates — §11.2 Shell is the sharpest, since P11-SHELL-CANCELLATION already asserts prompt cancellation — proving the abort reaches the side-effect owner, that awaited work reaches quiescence, and that a handler deriving a narrower deadline still aborts when the upstream cancellation fires

The schema exclusion is unchecked: OperationDescriptor.input accepts any JsonSchema, so nothing today refuses a declared input property that purports to carry cancellation, and nothing proves a handler cannot be reachable only through such a field. Verification requires the install-time manifest validation to refuse it, not the first invocation to fail on it

The durable-record boundary is satisfied by construction rather than by assertion, which is the direction a regression would come from: the ContentStore seam and the §8.5 command dispatcher take no signal, so an added one would silently widen this atom into the requirement it explicitly is not. A conformance assertion that those two seams stay cancellation-free is what keeps this rule from being read as requiring cancellation everywhere

Promotion to verified is blocked across a fragment boundary and the blocker is a true dependency rather than a bookkeeping accident: this row names C13-RECEIPT-FAILURE-KIND, which is W6's in invocations-audit.json and planned, so ledger.mjs's verified-status monotonicity rejects a verified row here until §7.4's failure-kind taxonomy is itself verified. An implemented status depending on a planned prerequisite is legal, and the dependency is real — the aborted-versus-indeterminate discrimination this atom exists to make is a claim about that taxonomy — so the edge stays and the promotion waits on W6 rather than being eased by dropping it

The implementation currently contradicts the rule and is the first thing that must change: src/facets/contribution.ts#OperationDescriptor declares `public readonly interceptable = false` and its codec lists interceptable among the REQUIRED fields, decoded through requireBoolean and re-emitted by toData(), so a withheld capability is today a mandatory present false both on the wire and in the manifest digest input. The presence-typed form has to replace it in the class, in the codec's required/optional split, and in toData() together, or one of the three keeps the negative encoding alive

Both readers test the flag for truth rather than for presence — src/composition/authority.ts#admitsInterception uses descriptor.interceptable and src/operations/interception.ts refuses on its negation — so both keep working after the change and neither discriminates. The clause with no implementation at all is the refusal: a manifest carrying interceptable false must be REFUSED at install rather than accepted as equivalent to absence, and that refusal needs its own case

The digest consequence is the reason the rule is stated and is unmeasured: two manifests differing only in a present false versus an absent key must be shown to produce one manifestDigest under the §5.2 PackagePin rather than two, so an inert declaration cannot change the release a RunPin names

The generality clause needs a conformance assertion rather than a case, because it forbids a negative encoding for every capability this document declares by presence: a check over the declared record shapes — terminal, failure, projectionDigest, duplicateOf, authenticationDigest — proving none has acquired a boolean or nullable form is what keeps the defect from reappearing elsewhere, and no current gate performs it

Mutation attribution needs two mutants, not one: flipping the install refusal to accept a present false must kill a cited test, and so must flipping the decoder to read absence as false and re-emit it, because the second is exactly how the negative form returns after the first is fixed

The declaration does not exist yet and its absence is enforced: src/facets/contribution.ts#OperationDescriptor carries no availability member and its codec's exact-field check would reject one, so the type, the codec's optional-field set, toData(), and the descriptor reconstruction in src/facets/profile-runtime/contract.ts all need the new member before any other clause can be asserted

The absent-means-native default needs discrimination and not merely a default value: a descriptor declaring no availability must be shown unreachable from agent-authored code, and a mutation defaulting it to both must break a cited test rather than silently widening every existing Operation into code mode

The one-set clause is the substance of the rule and has nothing to test against: nothing today computes the Bindings handed to a dynamic isolate, so verification needs that computation plus proof that its members are exactly the code- or both-available Operations the caller holds authority for, that a native-only Operation is not passable, and that the same declared set is what the offered catalog records under C13-TURN-MODEL-INPUT-RECONSTRUCTABLE — a host keeping two sets in agreement must fail

The composition clauses ride on atoms that are themselves planned: availability changed at the Scope mid-Turn must not change what that Turn's isolate reaches, which needs the captured FacetSet of C13-TURN-FACET-SET-STABLE, and the materialized availability record must appear in the declaring Facet's withdrawal set under C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT rather than surviving its contributor

The validation-time rejection is a definition-plane obligation with no current reader: the Blueprint validator does not relate policies.placement's consumer-to-backing mapping to any Operation's declared availability, so a code-available Operation on a platform that maps no backing and declares no default cannot be refused today. Closure requires that relation, the no-code-loaded assertion C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already tests against, and a discriminating case proving the failure lands at validation rather than at the first submission that needs the runtime

The contributor half exists for slot entries only: src/facets/slot-entry.ts#SlotEntry already carries `contributor: FacetRef` and derives its SlotEntryId from (slot, contributor, ordinal, value). Adding `package: PackagePin` changes that identity digest, so it requires a facet.slot-entry codec major past 2, decode rejection of an entry carrying no pin, and restore round-trips through MemoryWorkspaceSlotStore and the SQLite Workspace slot store

The other record kinds this rule names are unattributed today: catalog entries, derived Subscriptions, Surface registrations, prompt sections, ingress endpoints, and merged settings fragments carry neither a contributor nor a PackagePin. src/definition/materialization-kind.ts#validateSlotEntry admits exactly the keys contributor/index/slot/value, so the materializer's desired-state shape has to gain the pin before any of those kinds can be attributed

Same-transaction writing and lifetime immutability need discriminating evidence per kind. Slot entries are already immutable by encode-compare in both stores, but a record of another kind written without attribution must be rejected rather than accepted and backfilled, and rewriting a materialized record's contributor or pin must fail

Totality is the load-bearing claim and needs a negative test: a host that cannot attribute a contribution must refuse to materialize it, so that the withdrawal set of C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT is computable for every installed Facet by construction rather than by convention

Verification order, because a promoter reading only a dependent's own row would not see it: this atom has no prerequisites and roots the withdrawal family, so C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT depends on it directly and every atom depending on that one is transitively gated on it, spanning fragments owned by W3, W4, W5 and W7. Since the first obligation above is a facet.slot-entry codec major, no dependent reaches `verified` before a record codec version moves. Inbound edges are written by other owners in other fragments, so the dependent set must be re-derived at the promotion rev rather than trusted from this note

remainingEvidence: The declaration half exists and is already better keyed than a nominal string: src/facets/manifest.ts#BindingRequirement carries (name: BindingName, facet: FacetPackageId, compat: CompatRange) and round-trips through the facet manifest codec. Nothing consumes it as an activation precondition — no facet runtime in src/facets gates start on requirement resolution, so the whole ordering half of this atom is unbuilt

The activation gate needs a host that resolves every BindingRequirement to a live ResolvedFacet before calling start, and four discriminating mutations must each break a cited test: calling start with one requirement unresolved, starting a Facet degraded rather than leaving it inactive, reporting an unresolvable requirement as a runtime failure instead of a rejected install, and admitting a resolution whose ResolutionStamp is not current under C13-AUTH-RESOLUTION-LIFETIME

The reliance guard needs the withdrawal path of C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT first, then evidence that withdrawing a relied-upon Facet records a pending obligation under the C13-BLUEPRINT-CONVERGENCE shape instead of retiring its records, that the obligation discharges exactly when the last relying Facet goes inactive, and that the withdrawal is never rejected and never silently completed while reliance stands

The teardown-window clause is the clause most easily lost and needs its own two-Facet test: a dependent whose teardown its provider's withdrawal triggered must successfully resolve that provider from inside its own stop, which means the provider stays resolvable for the whole of its own teardown rather than being unresolvable from the first retirement

Exact-FacetRef keying needs an adversarial substitution: a second installed Facet answering the same BindingName and compatible FacetPackageId must neither satisfy an unresolved requirement nor discharge an existing reliance, so reliance tracks the exact provider a dependent reached rather than the capability name it asked for

Pre-load rejection is a definition-plane obligation with no current implementation: the Blueprint validator holds no reliance graph, so a reliance cycle and a retained Facet whose requirement names a withdrawn Facet cannot be refused today. Verification requires that graph built from the Blueprint's declared Bindings and the installed manifests' requirements, plus the no-code-loaded assertion C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already tests against

The independence-from-the-child-tree clause needs discrimination against the existing tree ordering: a Facet that is a child of the withdrawing Facet but relies on nothing it provides must not be held, and a Facet that relies on it but is not its child must be, so an implementation cannot satisfy this atom by reusing the stop-children-first order alone

remainingEvidence: §4.1 previously stated only that `start` is idempotent, and §13's NC-FACET-MANIFEST-RUNTIME records that facet loading is not modeled, so partial activation has neither an implementation nor a formal witness. Verification requires an activation path that materializes into records the host can retire whole

The discriminating case is a Facet whose `start` materializes some contributions and then throws: every record attributed to it must be absent afterwards, byte-compared against the Scope's records captured before the attempt, and the outcome must be a typed failed install rather than a live or half-live Facet
Retirement of a partial activation reuses the attributed withdrawal set, so this atom cannot be verified before its two prerequisites are; it has no independent retirement path and must not grow one

The no-retry clause needs adversarial coverage: retrying activation against a Scope whose prior partial effect was not retired must be refused, and a failed Facet must be shown to obstruct neither another Facet's activation nor another Facet's withdrawal

No drain exists because no withdrawal exists. Verification requires the withdrawal transaction to durably capture the finite set of admitted Invocation items whose PreparedInvocationHeader.target names the Facet, and to refuse completion while any captured item lacks a terminal current Receipt

Admission closure needs adversarial evidence on both sides: an Invocation prepared against the withdrawing Facet after the withdrawal transaction must be refused, and an item admitted before it must still settle against its frozen intent, placement, and Package pin across restart rather than against whatever later occupies that FacetRef

The reservation split must be shown exhaustive: a RouteReservation that reached preparation drains as one of these Invocation items, one the target has not admitted takes the terminal rejected RouteDelivery the withdrawal set requires, and no reservation falls in neither case. That half needs ownership-correct integration evidence with the W7 routing surface, which owns RouteDelivery

The prohibition is the part a passing test can hide: a host that reports a withdrawal complete by discarding, synthesizing, or shortcutting a draining item's Receipt must fail, and a mutation removing the drain gate must break a cited test rather than merely change timing

There is no withdrawal Operation in the runtime and no retirement path in the stores: src/facets/slot-memory.ts and src/substrates/sqlite/slot.ts expose insertSlot and insertEntry with immutable-entry enforcement and nothing that removes either. Verification requires an `administer` Operation whose control transaction retires the computed set, plus store-level retirement in the Memory and SQLite Workspace slot stores with snapshot and reopen round-trips

Exactness needs a two-contributor discriminating case: a Facet whose install materialized records under two PackagePins alongside a second Facet contributing into the same slots, where the withdrawal retires exactly the first Facet's records and leaves every record attributed to the second byte-identical. A withdrawal computed from anything other than attribution must fail that comparison

The authority half is entirely unbuilt: nothing retires a Binding naming a withdrawn FacetRef or a Grant whose capability names only the withdrawn Facet's Operations, and the Scope epoch advance those retirements must share with the Binding mutation transaction (§3.4 rule 5, C13-OWNERSHIP-AUTHORITY-RECORDS) has no withdrawal trigger to attach to

The Subscription liveness closure cannot be evidenced at the slot layer: it requires that no reservation be appended against a retired Subscription after the withdrawal transaction, and that every reservation already appended and not yet prepared reach a terminal rejected RouteDelivery written by the owning Actor. RouteDelivery belongs to the W7 routing surface, so this needs ownership-correct integration evidence rather than a W3 unit test

Both refusal cases need adversarial coverage with no partial effect: a withdrawal whose set the host cannot compute, and a withdrawal whose set holds a Slot declaration carrying an entry attributed to a Facet the same reconciliation retains, must each be refused atomically with every record left unchanged

Content retention needs a counterfactual rather than an assertion: retiring an attributed record that names a ContentRef must leave that content resolvable while any retained record still names it, and must never release a ContentRef a RunCommit or an admitted inbox Event names, so that C13-TURN-MODEL-INPUT-RECONSTRUCTABLE survives a withdrawal
